json-validator.use: Inspect an API response before adapting it in a script. Formatting makes nested values readable without rounding large numeric tokens.
json-validator.expected: Valid JSON. The large_integer token remains 9007199254740993 after formatting. Duplicate object keys are errors.

json-compare.use: Compare two saved API responses or configurations when spacing and object-key order should not count as changes.
json-compare.expected: Two modified paths: /enabled and /count. Numeric tokens are preserved; 1 and 1.0 are intentionally different.

csv-json-converter.use: Move a small table into JSON while preserving identifiers with leading zeros.
csv-json-converter.expected: CSV → JSON keeps "001" and "002" as strings. JSON → CSV has its own scalar-value and spreadsheet-safety rules.

csv-comparator.use: Check how an exported table changed between two snapshots using a unique identifier column.
csv-comparator.expected: With id as the identifier, record 2 is modified and record 1 is unchanged. The example above uses literal \n to show CSV line endings.

duplicate-finder.use: Find repeated record identifiers and distinguish identical repeats from conflicting string values.
duplicate-finder.expected: alpha and beta are repeated identifiers. Only alpha has conflicting values. Choose id and value as the fields.

text-diff.use: Compare small configuration snapshots or notes line by line before applying a change.
text-diff.expected: One removed line and one added line. Case and spaces matter; the presence of a final newline is reported separately.

regex-tester.use: Extract version-like tokens from a small text and inspect capture groups using the browser’s JavaScript engine.
regex-tester.input:
Pattern: v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)
Flags: g
Text: OpenViST v0.5.0
regex-tester.expected: One match: v0.5.0; captures 0, 5 and 0. This pattern matches a spelling, not full semantic-version validity.

code-to-image.use: Prepare a short, readable code illustration for documentation or a social post without running the snippet.
code-to-image.expected: A PNG containing the code as plain text. Style, title, line numbers and 1×/2× resolution can be changed. Syntax is not checked.

base64.use: Encode a short UTF-8 value for a documented data format, or decode a Base64 value for inspection.
base64.expected: Standard Base64 encoding produces SGVsbG8=. Decoding it as UTF-8 returns Hello. Base64 does not encrypt the text.
base64.recipe_note: These related scripts inspect UTF-8 input; they do not implement the Base64 tool.

url-encoder.use: Encode one query-parameter value or inspect repeated parameters in a saved URL without requesting that URL.
url-encoder.expected: Component encoding yields hello%20world%2B. Query inspection preserves both tag entries and decodes q as a b.
url-encoder.recipe_note: These scripts group or compare saved URL paths; their contracts differ from component encoding.

sha256-checksum.use: Compare the bytes of a downloaded file against a checksum obtained from a trusted source.
sha256-checksum.expected: SHA-256 of exactly these three UTF-8 bytes, without a newline: ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
sha256-checksum.recipe_note: The manifest recipe hashes files; the spelling classifier validates hexadecimal text and does not calculate hashes.

sitemap-inspector.use: Inspect a saved sitemap for repeated URLs and structural issues before doing a separate live-link audit.
sitemap-inspector.expected: One URL entry and no duplicates. This tool does not fetch the URL or establish whether Google will index it.
